blocks.html: Correlation gave one number, r = 0.82, for how strongly age and weight move together in the under-five clinic register (recall §11.2). Regression turns that into an equation: how much weight changes, on average, per month of age, and what weight to expect for a given child. This chapter builds simple linear regression from the least-squares principle, then extends it to several predictors, to curved relationships, and to the diagnostic checks that tell you whether a fitted model can be trusted. Regression inherits every caution of §11.5: a coefficient describes an association in the data, and calling it an effect needs the same extra evidence as any correlation. Chapter 13 (generalised linear models, regression for binary and count outcomes) extends the same framework.
